_meta.author: Eduventure (original questions)
_meta.note: Primary batch 1: Maths 20, Science 15, English 15, including the new question types. In review until approved in /admin. Contains answers: never imported by src/.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Which number is 1,000 more than 3,456?
questions.explanation: Adding 1,000 changes only the thousands digit: 3 thousands become 4 thousands, so 3,456 becomes 4,456.
questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: whole numbers to 10,000 (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 3–4).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: What is 6 × 7?

mistakes.why: 48 is 6 × 8, one group of 6 too many.
36 is 6 × 6, one group of 6 too few.

questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: multiplication facts (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 3).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: What is 144 ÷ 12?

mistakes.why: 132 is 144 − 12; division asks how many 12s fit into 144.

questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: division (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 4).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Select all the multiples of 4.
questions.explanation: 12 = 4 × 3, 20 = 4 × 5 and 36 = 4 × 9, so they are multiples of 4.

wrong.b: 18 ÷ 4 = 4 remainder 2, so 18 is not a multiple of 4.
wrong.d: 30 ÷ 4 = 7 remainder 2, so 30 is not a multiple of 4.

questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: factors and multiples (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 5).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Put these fractions in order from smallest to largest.
questions.explanation: With the same top number, more equal pieces means smaller pieces: 1/8 < 1/4 < 1/2.
questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: fractions (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 3–4).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Match each shape to its number of sides.
questions.explanation: Triangle: 3 sides. Pentagon: 5 ("penta" means five). Octagon: 8 ("octo" means eight, like an octopus's arms).
questions.objective: Name polygons by their number of sides.
questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: 2D shapes (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 2–4).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: What is 3/5 written as a percentage?

wrong.a: 35% just joins the digits 3 and 5; 3/5 means 3 out of 5 equal parts.
wrong.c: 53% swaps the digits; 3 out of 5 is more than half, i.e. 60%.

questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: percentages (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 5–6).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: A bus has 48 seats. 29 seats are taken. How many seats are empty?
questions.explanation: Empty seats = total − taken = 48 − 29 = 19.

mistakes.why: 77 adds the numbers; we need what is left after the taken seats, so subtract.
Check the borrowing: 48 − 29 = 19 (48 − 30 = 18, then add 1 back).

questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: subtraction problem solving (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 3).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Which of these numbers is a prime number?
questions.explanation: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 29 cannot be divided evenly by any other whole number.

wrong.a: 21 = 3 × 7, so it has more than two factors.
wrong.d: 33 = 3 × 11, so it is not prime.

questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: number properties (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 5–6).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: How many millilitres are there in 2.5 litres?

mistakes.why: There are 1,000 ml in a litre, not 100.

questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: volume of liquid (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 4–5).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: True or false: 0.7 is greater than 0.65.
questions.explanation: Write both with two decimal places: 0.70 and 0.65. Seventy hundredths is more than sixty-five hundredths.

wrong.false: Having more digits does not make a decimal bigger. Compare place by place: 7 tenths beats 6 tenths.

questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: decimals (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 4–5).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: What is the next number in the pattern 3, 7, 11, 15, …?
questions.explanation: Each number is 4 more than the one before, so 15 + 4 = 19.

mistakes.why: The pattern adds 4 each time, not 3.

questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: number patterns (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 2–3).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: How many degrees are there in a right angle?
questions.explanation: A right angle is a quarter turn: 90°. The corner of a book is a right angle.

wrong.c: 180° is a straight line (a half turn).
wrong.d: 360° is a full turn.

questions.objective: Know the size of a right angle.
questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: angles (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 4–5).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: A square has sides of 7 cm. What is its area in square centimetres?
questions.explanation: Area of a square = side × side = 7 × 7 = 49 cm².

mistakes.why: 28 cm is the perimeter (4 × 7), not the area.
14 is 7 + 7; area multiplies the two sides.

questions.objective: Calculate the area of a square.
questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: area (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 4–5).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Put these times in order from earliest to latest in the same day.
questions.explanation: a.m. times are before noon and p.m. times are after noon: 9:40 a.m., then 11:05 a.m., then 1:15 p.m.
questions.objective: Order times using a.m. and p.m.
questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: time (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 3–4).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Round 6.48 to the nearest whole number.
questions.explanation: Look at the tenths digit: 4 is less than 5, so round down to 6.

wrong.b: 6.5 is rounded to one decimal place, not to a whole number.
wrong.c: Only round up when the tenths digit is 5 or more; here it is 4.
wrong.d: 6.4 keeps a decimal place; a whole number has none.

questions.objective: Round decimals to the nearest whole number.
questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: decimals (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 5).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Amir buys 3 notebooks that cost RM2.50 each. How much does he pay, in ringgit?

mistakes.why: That adds 3 to the price; he buys 3 notebooks, so multiply by 3.

questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: money (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 4).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: What do we call a triangle whose three sides are all the same length?
questions.explanation: An equilateral triangle has three equal sides (and three equal 60° angles). "Equi" means equal and "lateral" means side.
questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: properties of 2D shapes (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 5–6).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Select all the shapes that have exactly four sides.
questions.explanation: Squares, rectangles and rhombuses are all quadrilaterals: shapes with four straight sides.
questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: 2D shapes (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 3–4).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: What is 1/4 of 60?
questions.explanation: One quarter means dividing into 4 equal parts: 60 ÷ 4 = 15.

mistakes.why: 240 is 60 × 4; finding a quarter means dividing by 4.
30 is one half of 60, not one quarter.

questions.objective: Find a unit fraction of a quantity.
questions.alignment: Primary mathematics: fractions of quantities (e.g. KSSR Matematik Tahun 4).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which part of a plant takes in water from the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots grow into the soil, hold the plant in place and absorb water and minerals.

wrong.b: Leaves make food using sunlight; they lose water rather than take it from the soil.
wrong.d: Fruit protects seeds and helps spread them.

questions.objective: Describe the functions of the parts of a plant.
questions.alignment: Primary science: plants (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 1–3).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Select all the living things.
questions.explanation: Living things grow, need food and water, respond to their surroundings and reproduce. Mushrooms (fungi), ferns (plants) and beetles (animals) all do.

wrong.b: A rock does not grow, feed or reproduce.
wrong.d: Living things need water, but water itself is not alive.

questions.objective: Classify things as living or non-living.
questions.alignment: Primary science: living things (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 1–2).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: True or false: the Moon makes its own light.
questions.explanation: The Moon shines because it reflects light from the Sun. That is why we see different phases as different parts are lit.

wrong.true: The Moon has no light of its own; moonlight is sunlight bouncing off its surface.

questions.objective: Explain why the Moon appears bright.
questions.alignment: Primary science: the solar system (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 5–6).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which gas do we breathe out more of than we breathe in?
questions.explanation: Our cells use oxygen and produce carbon dioxide as waste, so the air we breathe out has more carbon dioxide.

wrong.a: We breathe out less oxygen than we breathe in, because our body uses some.
wrong.c: Nitrogen passes in and out almost unchanged.
wrong.d: There is hardly any helium in air, and our body does not make it.

questions.objective: Describe the gases involved in breathing.
questions.alignment: Primary science: human body systems (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 4–5).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Put the stages of a butterfly's life cycle in order, starting from the beginning.
questions.explanation: Egg → caterpillar → pupa → adult. This big change in body shape is called complete metamorphosis.
questions.objective: Sequence the stages of an insect life cycle.
questions.alignment: Primary science: life cycles (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 2–3).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Match each animal to the group it belongs to.
questions.explanation: Frogs are amphibians (they start life in water), eagles are birds (feathers, beaks) and snakes are reptiles (dry, scaly skin).
questions.alignment: Primary science: classification of animals (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 3–4).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What is the name of the force that pulls objects towards the Earth?
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls everything towards the Earth's centre. It is why a dropped ball falls down.
questions.alignment: Primary science: forces (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 5–6).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which of these is a source of light?
questions.explanation: A light source makes its own light. The Sun gives off light; the others only reflect or let light through.

wrong.b: A mirror reflects light but does not make it.
wrong.c: The Moon reflects sunlight; it is not a light source.
wrong.d: A window lets light pass through; it does not make light.

questions.alignment: Primary science: light (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 4).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What do we call animals that eat only plants?
questions.explanation: Herbivores (like cows and rabbits) eat only plants.

wrong.c: Omnivores eat both plants and animals.
wrong.d: Predators hunt other animals for food.

questions.objective: Classify animals by what they eat.
questions.alignment: Primary science: animals and their food (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 2–3).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: True or false: metals are generally good conductors of heat.
questions.explanation: Heat moves through metals quickly. That is why a metal spoon in hot soup soon feels hot, while a wooden spoon does not.

wrong.false: Metals let heat pass through easily; materials like wood and plastic are the poor conductors (insulators).

questions.objective: Classify materials as heat conductors or insulators.
questions.alignment: Primary science: materials (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 5).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which organs help us breathe?
questions.explanation: The lungs take oxygen from the air into the blood and remove carbon dioxide.

wrong.b: Kidneys clean the blood and make urine.
wrong.c: The liver processes nutrients and removes harmful substances.
wrong.d: The stomach helps digest food.

questions.alignment: Primary science: human body (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 3–4).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: When water vapour cools down and turns back into liquid water, the process is called ___.
questions.explanation: Condensation is gas turning into liquid when it cools, like droplets forming on a cold glass. It is how clouds form in the water cycle.
questions.objective: Describe processes in the water cycle.
questions.alignment: Primary science: water cycle (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 5).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: About how long does the Earth take to travel once around the Sun?
questions.explanation: One orbit of the Sun takes about 365¼ days: one year.

wrong.a: One day is how long the Earth takes to spin once on its own axis.
wrong.b: A week has no link to the Earth's orbit.
wrong.c: About a month is how long the Moon takes to orbit the Earth.

questions.objective: Relate day and year to the Earth's movement.
questions.alignment: Primary science: the Earth and the Sun (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 5–6).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Select all the objects that a magnet will attract.
questions.explanation: Magnets attract iron and materials containing iron, such as steel.

wrong.d: Wood is not magnetic.
wrong.e: Aluminium is a metal, but it is not attracted to magnets. Not all metals are magnetic.

questions.alignment: Primary science: magnets (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 2–3).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why do we usually see lightning before we hear thunder?

options.text: Light travels much faster than sound
The lightning happens before the thunder is made
Our eyes are closer to the sky than our ears

questions.explanation: Lightning and thunder happen together, but light reaches us almost instantly while sound travels about 343 metres per second, so the thunder arrives later.

wrong.b: It is the other way round: light is about a million times faster than sound.
wrong.c: Thunder is the sound of the lightning itself; both happen at the same moment.
wrong.d: The tiny difference in where our eyes and ears are cannot cause a delay of seconds.

questions.objective: Compare the speed of light and sound.
questions.alignment: Primary science: light and sound (e.g. KSSR Sains Tahun 4–5).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: ___ elephant is very big.
questions.explanation: We use "an" before words that begin with a vowel sound: an elephant, an apple.

wrong.a: "A" goes before consonant sounds (a dog); "elephant" starts with a vowel sound.
wrong.c: "Much" is used with things we cannot count, like water.
wrong.d: "Few" goes with plural nouns (few elephants).

questions.objective: Use the articles a and an correctly.
questions.alignment: Primary English: grammar – articles (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What is the past tense of "eat"?
questions.explanation: "Eat" is irregular: eat → ate → eaten. Yesterday I ate rice.

wrong.a: "Eated" is not a word; "eat" does not use -ed.
wrong.c: "Eaten" needs a helper: I have eaten.
wrong.d: "Eating" shows an action in progress.

questions.objective: Use the past tense of irregular verbs.
questions.alignment: Primary English: grammar – past tense (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Select all the nouns in this sentence: "The dog chased a ball in the park."
questions.explanation: Nouns name people, animals, places or things: dog (animal), ball (thing), park (place).

wrong.b: "Chased" is a verb: it is the action.
wrong.d: "In" is a preposition: it tells us where.

questions.alignment: Primary English: grammar – word classes (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Put these words in alphabetical order.
questions.explanation: Look at the first letters: a comes before l, and l comes before m. So: apple, lemon, mango.
questions.alignment: Primary English: dictionary skills (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Match each word to its opposite.
questions.explanation: Opposites (antonyms): hot – cold, tall – short, happy – sad.
questions.alignment: Primary English: vocabulary (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What is the plural of "mouse" (the small animal)?
questions.explanation: "Mouse" has an irregular plural: one mouse, two mice.
questions.alignment: Primary English: grammar – nouns (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which of these sentences is a question?

options.text: What a big bag this is!

questions.explanation: A question asks something and ends with a question mark.

wrong.b: This is a statement: it tells us something.
wrong.c: This is a command: it tells someone to do something.
wrong.d: This is an exclamation: it shows a strong feeling and ends with !

questions.alignment: Primary English: sentence types (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which word is the verb in this sentence? "The children sing loudly."
questions.explanation: A verb is an action or doing word. "Sing" is what the children do.

wrong.b: "Children" is a noun: it names who.
wrong.d: "Loudly" is an adverb: it tells how they sing.

questions.alignment: Primary English: grammar – word classes (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A statement starts with a capital letter and ends with a full ___.
questions.explanation: A statement ends with a full stop (.). In American English it is called a period.
questions.alignment: Primary English: punctuation (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with "cat"?
questions.explanation: Rhyming words end with the same sound: c-at, h-at.

wrong.d: "Cap" starts the same way but ends in -ap.

questions.alignment: Primary English: phonics (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: True or false: "quickly" is an adverb.
questions.explanation: Adverbs describe how, when or where something happens. "Quickly" tells us how an action is done, and many adverbs end in -ly.

wrong.false: "Quickly" describes a verb (She ran quickly), which is exactly what an adverb does.

questions.alignment: Primary English: grammar – word classes (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: "Because" is spelled b-e-c-a-u-s-e. A memory trick: Big Elephants Can Always Understand Small Elephants.

wrong.a: The letters a and u are swapped.
wrong.c: There is no o in because.
wrong.d: There is an extra a: it is be-cause, not bea-cause.

questions.alignment: Primary English: spelling (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What does the word "enormous" mean?
questions.explanation: "Enormous" means extremely large, like an enormous whale.

wrong.b: "Very small" is the opposite; that would be "tiny".
wrong.d: "Very quiet" would be "silent".

questions.objective: Understand the meaning of new words.
questions.alignment: Primary English: vocabulary (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: She is ___ than her brother.
questions.explanation: When comparing two people with "than", short adjectives add -er: taller.

wrong.a: "Tall" does not compare; we need the -er form before "than".
wrong.c: "Tallest" compares three or more: the tallest in the class.
wrong.d: Short adjectives like "tall" use -er, not "more".

questions.alignment: Primary English: grammar – adjectives (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Write the short form (contraction) of "do not".
questions.explanation: "Do not" becomes "don't": the apostrophe replaces the missing letter o.
questions.alignment: Primary English: grammar – contractions (e.g. KSSR Bahasa Inggeris).
